registry_info.name: vectors
registry_info.description: Vector operation artifacts - addition, subtraction, magnitude, normalization, dot product, cross product, projection
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Linear algebra fundamentals, 3D graphics programming, physics simulation

hl_turret_vectors.name: Half-Life Turret - Vector Compendium
hl_turret_vectors.description: Half-Life inspired sentry turret demonstrating ALL vector operations in one coherent system: subtraction (direction to target), magnitude (distance/range check), normalization (unit direction), dot product (FOV check), cross product (rotation axis), projection (ground plane), scalar multiplication (bullet velocity), and velocity integration (bullet physics). Fires tracer rounds with visible velocity vectors!
hl_turret_vectors.qfep_connection: The turret as computational subject - vectors as the mathematics of surveillance, targeting, and ballistics. Shows how abstract math operations have immediate, embodied applications in games and simulations.
interactions: grab target sphere to move it

parameters.show_bullet_vectors: Show velocity arrows on bullets (default true)

vector_addition_demo.name: Vector Addition
vector_addition_demo.description: Interactive vector addition visualizer: A + B = C. Shows parallelogram law with head-to-tail placement and ghost arrows.
vector_addition_demo.qfep_connection: Composition - how separate movements combine into a single displacement
interactions: grab handle spheres to adjust vectors

vector_subtraction_demo.name: Vector Subtraction
vector_subtraction_demo.description: Interactive vector subtraction: A - B = C. Shows how subtraction finds the difference vector between two points.
vector_subtraction_demo.qfep_connection: Difference and direction - finding what separates two states

vector_magnitude_demo.name: Vector Magnitude
vector_magnitude_demo.description: Visualizes vector magnitude (length) using Pythagorean theorem. Shows |V| = √(x² + y² + z²).
vector_magnitude_demo.qfep_connection: Measurement - quantifying the 'amount' of a vector regardless of direction

vector_normalize_demo.name: Vector Normalization
vector_normalize_demo.description: Shows normalization: V̂ = V/|V|. Converts any vector to unit length while preserving direction.
vector_normalize_demo.qfep_connection: Pure direction - stripping magnitude to reveal only orientation

dot_product_projector.name: Dot Product Projector
dot_product_projector.description: Interactive dot product visualizer showing A · B = |A||B|cos(θ). Demonstrates projection and alignment measurement.
dot_product_projector.qfep_connection: Dot product as alignment - measuring how much two directions agree or oppose

cross_product_demo.name: Cross Product Demo
cross_product_demo.description: Interactive cross product: A × B produces a vector perpendicular to both. Shows parallelogram area and right-hand rule.
cross_product_demo.qfep_connection: Cross product as emergence - a third direction arising from two, perpendicularity as difference

vector_projection_demo.name: Vector Projection
vector_projection_demo.description: Visualizes vector projection onto another vector or plane. Shows shadow/component decomposition.
vector_projection_demo.qfep_connection: Projection as filtering - extracting the component in a particular direction

vector_translation_demo.name: Vector Translation
vector_translation_demo.description: Shows vectors as displacements in space. Position vectors and translation vectors.
vector_translation_demo.qfep_connection: Translation as movement - vectors as instructions for displacement

basis_vectors_rig.name: Basis Vectors Rig
basis_vectors_rig.description: Interactive basis vectors (î, ĵ, k̂) showing how any 3D point is a linear combination: P = xî + yĵ + zk̂.
basis_vectors_rig.qfep_connection: Basis as frame of reference - the coordinate system from which we measure all positions

parameters.target_point: Point to decompose into basis components

turret_targeting.name: Turret Targeting (Combined)
turret_targeting.description: Combined turret + ball dropper setup. Laser turret tracks and destroys falling balls. Use laser_turret and ball_dropper separately for custom arrangements.
turret_targeting.qfep_connection: Targeting as embodied vector math - the turret performs subtraction, normalization, and dot product continuously to track moving targets.

parameters.dropper_offset: Offset of ball dropper from turret (default 0,3,2)

laser_turret.name: Laser Turret
laser_turret.description: Standalone laser turret that auto-targets and destroys balls. Place separately from ball_dropper to customize layout. Demonstrates vector subtraction (direction), magnitude (range), normalization (aim), dot product (lock).
laser_turret.qfep_connection: The turret as computational subject - continuously computing direction vectors to track moving targets.
interactions: Automatic targeting - no direct interaction needed

ball_dropper.name: Ball Dropper
ball_dropper.description: Drops colorful physics balls one at a time. Pair with laser_turret for targeting demo. Balls cycle through colors and have configurable physics properties.
ball_dropper.qfep_connection: Entropy source - introducing moving targets into the system for the turret to track.

sentry_turret.name: Sentry Turret
sentry_turret.description: Half-Life style sentry turret. Targets balls and/or player. Simple reliable targeting with bullet physics. Emits signals for hits.
sentry_turret.qfep_connection: The turret as autonomous agent - continuously computing vectors to track and engage targets.

turret_boll_infoboard.name: Turret-Boll Vector Diagram
turret_boll_infoboard.description: 3m × 6m semi-transparent infoboard showing ALL vector operations in one static diagram: subtraction (direction), magnitude (range), normalization (aim), dot product (lock), projection (prediction). Visual reference for turret targeting math.
turret_boll_infoboard.qfep_connection: The diagram as pedagogical synthesis - all vector operations unified through the targeting metaphor, showing how abstract math becomes embodied behavior.

vector_joint_playground.name: Vector-Joint Playground
vector_joint_playground.description: Human-scale VR playground with 6 interactive stations. Each station pairs draggable vectors with a large physics joint mechanism: crane (magnitude), pistons (addition), door (dot product), seesaw (subtraction), waterwheel (cross product), spring tower (forces). Drag a vector, watch the machine respond.
vector_joint_playground.qfep_connection: Vectors as embodied forces — abstract math becomes physical machinery that moves, tilts, spins, and bounces at human scale
interactions: read live math on info panels

vector_field_visualizer.name: Vector Field Visualizer
vector_field_visualizer.description: 3D arrow field showing flow — vortex, source, sink, or dipole fields. An 8x8x4 grid of arrow glyphs colored by magnitude (blue=slow, red=fast). Each arrow drawn with ImmediateMesh lines for shaft and arrowhead.
vector_field_visualizer.qfep_connection: Vector fields as continuous flow — every point in space carries a direction, the field as a living topology of force and movement.

coordinate_system_switcher.name: Coordinate System Switcher
coordinate_system_switcher.description: Shows the same 3D point in Cartesian (x,y,z), Cylindrical (r,θ,z), and Spherical (ρ,θ,φ) coordinates simultaneously. ImmediateMesh axes and arcs with projection lines showing how each system maps. Color-coded: Cartesian=RGB, Cylindrical=yellow, Spherical=magenta.
coordinate_system_switcher.qfep_connection: Multiple coordinate systems as multiple perspectives on the same reality — the point doesn't change, only the language describing it.
